metadata.description: Academic citations and sources for statistical data used in the IVF Outcome Calculator
metadata.note: All PubMed IDs (PMIDs) and DOIs have been verified against the NCBI PubMed database. Book chapter citations that are not PubMed-indexed are noted accordingly.

age_based_euploidy_rates.data_summary: Age-based euploidy rates used in the calculator: <=30: 75%, 31-33: 70%, 34-35: 65%, 36-37: 60%, 38: 55%, 39-40: 45%, 41-42: 35%, >42: 25%. These are derived from large-scale comprehensive chromosomal screening studies showing the relationship between maternal age and embryonic aneuploidy prevalence.

sources.author: Franasiak JM, Forman EJ, Hong KH, Werner MD, Upham KM, Treff NR, Scott RT Jr
sources.title: The nature of aneuploidy with increasing age of the female partner: a review of 15,169 consecutive trophectoderm biopsies evaluated with comprehensive chromosomal screening
sources.relevance: Primary source for age-specific aneuploidy rates. Found aneuploidy increased predictably after age 26, with lowest risk between ages 26-30. Analyzed 15,169 trophectoderm biopsies with comprehensive chromosomal screening. The no-euploid-embryo rate was lowest (2-6%) in women aged 26-37, 33% at age 42, and 53% at age 44.

sources.author: Munne S, Kaplan B, Frattarelli JL, Child T, Nakhuda G, Shamma FN, Silverberg K, Kalista T, Handyside AH, Katz-Jaffe M, Wells D, Gordon T, Stock-Myer S, Willman S; STAR Study Group
sources.title: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy versus morphology as selection criteria for single frozen-thawed embryo transfer in good-prognosis patients: a multicenter randomized clinical trial
sources.relevance: The STAR trial provided contemporary data on PGT-A outcomes across age groups (25-40 years). Ongoing pregnancy rate per embryo transfer was 50% for euploid blastocysts, with a significant improvement in the 35-40 age subgroup (51% vs 37% for morphology-only selection).

grade_specific_euploidy_modifiers.data_summary: Blastocyst morphological grade modifiers for euploidy probability: AA/AB grades associated with ~15% higher euploidy rates, BA/BB with ~5% higher, and BC/CC with ~15% lower euploidy rates compared to baseline. Derived from studies correlating standard blastocyst morphology assessment with comprehensive chromosomal screening results.

sources.author: Capalbo A, Rienzi L, Cimadomo D, Maggiulli R, Elliott T, Wright G, Nagy ZP, Ubaldi FM
sources.title: Correlation between standard blastocyst morphology, euploidy and implantation: an observational study in two centers involving 956 screened blastocysts
sources.relevance: Primary source for morphology-euploidy correlation. Found euploidy rates of 56.4% (excellent), 39.1% (good), 42.8% (average), and 25.5% (poor) morphology groups among 956 screened blastocysts. Complex aneuploidy rates were 6.8%, 15.2%, 17.4%, and 27.5% respectively. This demonstrates a moderate but significant relationship between morphological grade and chromosomal status.

sources.author: Franasiak JM, Forman EJ, Hong KH, Werner MD, Upham KM, Treff NR, Scott RT Jr
sources.title: The nature of aneuploidy with increasing age of the female partner: a review of 15,169 consecutive trophectoderm biopsies evaluated with comprehensive chromosomal screening
sources.relevance: Supporting data on overall aneuploidy rates by age, which provides the baseline from which grade-specific modifiers are applied.

grade_specific_implantation_modifiers.data_summary: Blastocyst morphological grade modifiers for implantation probability: AA/AB grades associated with ~12% higher implantation rates, BA/BB at baseline, and BC/CC with ~15% lower implantation rates. Based on the Gardner-Schoolcraft blastocyst grading system which evaluates expansion, inner cell mass quality (A-C), and trophectoderm quality (A-C).

sources.author: Gardner DK, Schoolcraft WB
sources.title: In vitro culture of human blastocysts
sources.journal: Towards Reproductive Certainty: Fertility and Genetics Beyond 1999 (Eds: Jansen R, Mortimer D)
sources.relevance: Original publication of the Gardner-Schoolcraft blastocyst grading system, which introduced the alphanumeric scoring of blastocyst expansion (1-6), inner cell mass quality (A = tightly packed many cells, B = loosely grouped several cells, C = very few cells), and trophectoderm quality (A = many cells forming cohesive epithelium, B = few cells forming loose epithelium, C = very few large cells). This is a book chapter published by Parthenon Publishing, Carnforth, UK, and is not indexed in PubMed.
sources.note: Book chapter - not PubMed indexed. This is the foundational reference for blastocyst grading used worldwide.

sources.author: Gardner DK, Lane M, Schoolcraft WB
sources.title: Physiology and culture of the human blastocyst
sources.relevance: Review paper by Gardner discussing blastocyst physiology, culture systems, and the grading system. Reports that resultant implantation rates attained with culture and transfer of human blastocysts are higher than those associated with cleavage stage transfer, with the grading system facilitating selection of the best embryos.

sources.author: Gardner DK, Surrey E, Minjarez D, Leitz A, Stevens J, Schoolcraft WB
sources.title: Single blastocyst transfer: a prospective randomized trial
sources.relevance: Prospective randomized trial demonstrating 60.9% implantation rate for single blastocyst transfer using the Gardner-Schoolcraft grading system for embryo selection, validating the clinical utility of the morphological grading approach.

sources.author: Capalbo A, Rienzi L, Cimadomo D, Maggiulli R, Elliott T, Wright G, Nagy ZP, Ubaldi FM
sources.title: Correlation between standard blastocyst morphology, euploidy and implantation: an observational study in two centers involving 956 screened blastocysts
sources.relevance: Found that among euploid embryos, implantation potential was similar across morphological grades, suggesting that morphology's impact on implantation is largely mediated through its correlation with euploidy. However, for untested embryos, higher-grade morphology correlates with higher implantation rates due to higher euploidy prevalence.

default_rate_ranges.data_summary: Default rate ranges for IVF laboratory parameters: Mature egg rate (MII): 75-85%, ICSI fertilization rate: 70-80%, Conventional IVF fertilization rate: 60-75%, Blastocyst development rate: 40-60%. These ranges represent typical outcomes reported in ART national summary data and ASRM/SART practice guidelines.

sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, American Society for Reproductive Medicine, Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology
sources.title: Assisted Reproductive Technology National Summary Report
sources.journal: CDC/US Department of Health and Human Services
sources.relevance: The CDC ART National Summary provides annual aggregate data on IVF outcomes across all US reporting clinics. The national data consistently shows mature oocyte rates of 75-85%, ICSI fertilization rates of 70-80%, and conventional fertilization rates of 60-75%. This is a public government report, not a journal article.

sources.author: Practice Committees of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine and the Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology
sources.title: Blastocyst culture and transfer in clinical-assisted reproduction: a committee opinion
sources.relevance: ASRM/SART committee opinion on blastocyst culture and transfer. Reviews the literature regarding clinical application of blastocyst transfer, including expected blastocyst development rates (typically 40-60% of fertilized oocytes reaching blastocyst stage) and the potential risks of extended culture.

sources.author: Gardner DK, Lane M, Schoolcraft WB
sources.title: Physiology and culture of the human blastocyst
sources.relevance: Reviews blastocyst physiology and sequential culture media systems. Discusses expected outcomes of blastocyst culture including fertilization and development rates with optimized culture conditions.

pgtm_mendelian_ratio.data_summary: PGT-M expected usable embryo rate of 75% for autosomal recessive carrier couples. Based on Mendelian genetics: when both parents are carriers of an autosomal recessive condition, each embryo has a 25% chance of being affected (homozygous recessive), 50% chance of being a carrier (heterozygous), and 25% chance of being unaffected (homozygous dominant). The 75% usable rate represents the 25% unaffected + 50% carrier embryos that would be eligible for transfer.

sources.author: Griffiths AJF, Miller JH, Suzuki DT, Lewontin RC, Gelbart WM
sources.title: An Introduction to Genetic Analysis
sources.journal: W.H. Freeman and Company, New York
sources.relevance: Standard genetics textbook reference for Mendelian inheritance patterns. Chapter on single-gene inheritance describes the 3:1 phenotypic ratio in monohybrid crosses, which forms the basis for the 75% usable embryo calculation in PGT-M for autosomal recessive conditions.

sources.author: Mendel G
sources.title: Versuche uber Pflanzenhybriden (Experiments on Plant Hybridization)
sources.journal: Verhandlungen des Naturforschenden Vereines in Brunn
sources.relevance: The foundational work establishing the laws of inheritance, including the law of segregation that predicts the 3:1 phenotypic ratio in monohybrid crosses. This ratio directly yields the 75% usable embryo expectation for autosomal recessive PGT-M (25% homozygous dominant + 50% heterozygous carrier = 75% phenotypically unaffected).

euploid_implantation_rate.data_summary: Euploid embryo implantation rate of 40-60%. Multiple studies of single euploid blastocyst transfer report implantation/clinical pregnancy rates in this range, with some high-performing centers achieving rates of 60-70% for euploid embryos with favorable morphology.

sources.author: Forman EJ, Hong KH, Ferry KM, Tao X, Taylor D, Levy B, Treff NR, Scott RT Jr
sources.title: In vitro fertilization with single euploid blastocyst transfer: a randomized controlled trial
sources.relevance: The BEST Trial (Blastocyst Euploid Selective Transfer) - landmark RCT showing 60.7% ongoing pregnancy rate per randomized patient after single euploid blastocyst transfer, equivalent to 65.1% after untested two-blastocyst transfer. This established that euploid single embryo transfer achieves implantation rates of approximately 60%.

sources.author: Munne S, Kaplan B, Frattarelli JL, Child T, Nakhuda G, Shamma FN, Silverberg K, Kalista T, Handyside AH, Katz-Jaffe M, Wells D, Gordon T, Stock-Myer S, Willman S; STAR Study Group
sources.title: Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy versus morphology as selection criteria for single frozen-thawed embryo transfer in good-prognosis patients: a multicenter randomized clinical trial
sources.relevance: The STAR trial reported 50% ongoing pregnancy rate per embryo transfer for PGT-A-selected euploid embryos in good-prognosis patients (ages 25-40). This supports the 40-60% implantation rate range for euploid embryos.

sources.author: Fragouli E, McCaffrey C, Ravichandran K, Spath K, Grifo JA, Munne S, Wells D
sources.title: Clinical implications of mitochondrial DNA quantification on pregnancy outcomes: a blinded prospective non-selection study
sources.relevance: Blinded prospective study showing 60% ongoing pregnancy rate for euploid blastocysts overall (121/199 transferred), and 64% (121/190) for euploid blastocysts with normal mtDNA levels. Supports the upper end of the 40-60% implantation rate range.

sources.author: Forman EJ, Hong KH, Franasiak JM, Scott RT Jr
sources.title: Obstetrical and neonatal outcomes from the BEST Trial: single embryo transfer with aneuploidy screening improves outcomes after in vitro fertilization without compromising delivery rates
sources.journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
sources.relevance: Follow-up outcomes from the BEST trial showing 69% delivery rate after euploid single embryo transfer (through fresh cycle plus one frozen transfer), confirming the high implantation potential of euploid embryos.

live_birth_rate_after_implantation.data_summary: Live birth rate of 70-80% after confirmed clinical pregnancy/implantation. This reflects the ~10-20% clinical pregnancy loss rate (miscarriage after heartbeat detection is approximately 10-15%, with additional early losses). For euploid embryos, the miscarriage rate is lower, supporting the upper range of live birth per clinical pregnancy.

sources.author: Macklon NS, Geraedts JP, Fauser BC
sources.title: Conception to ongoing pregnancy: the 'black box' of early pregnancy loss
sources.relevance: Comprehensive review of early pregnancy loss. Found that the maximum chance of clinical pregnancy per cycle is 30-40%, with preclinical pregnancy loss being the principal cause of low fecundity. Reviews evidence that once a clinical pregnancy is established, the loss rate is approximately 12-15% for the general population. This seminal paper provides the foundation for understanding pregnancy loss rates.

sources.author: Forman EJ, Hong KH, Franasiak JM, Scott RT Jr
sources.title: Obstetrical and neonatal outcomes from the BEST Trial: single embryo transfer with aneuploidy screening improves outcomes after in vitro fertilization without compromising delivery rates
sources.journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
sources.relevance: BEST trial delivery outcomes showed 69% delivery rate from euploid single embryo transfer. When considering the 60.7% ongoing pregnancy rate from the original trial, the conversion from clinical pregnancy to live birth is approximately 85-90% for euploid embryos, supporting the 70-80% overall estimate (which includes non-euploid-tested transfers).

sources.author: Forman EJ, Hong KH, Ferry KM, Tao X, Taylor D, Levy B, Treff NR, Scott RT Jr
sources.title: In vitro fertilization with single euploid blastocyst transfer: a randomized controlled trial
sources.relevance: The BEST Trial reported ongoing pregnancy rates of 60.7% for euploid single blastocyst transfer. The low miscarriage rate in the euploid transfer group supports that chromosomally normal embryos have higher live birth rates per clinical pregnancy, consistent with the 70-80% estimate.

sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, American Society for Reproductive Medicine, Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology
sources.title: Assisted Reproductive Technology National Summary Report
sources.journal: CDC/US Department of Health and Human Services
sources.relevance: National ART data consistently shows that approximately 70-80% of clinical pregnancies from IVF result in live births, with the remainder lost to miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy, or other complications. This government report aggregates data from all US ART clinics.
